cues.text: Frame 0, close and settled, a kitchen: the homeowner left, on the phone, cross, the plumber right with the clipboard (she was at work and phoned). Up top, big: EVERY $100 in gold, under it in red: ALL HIS?. At 0.5 s a plain cut to her alone, close, on the phone (the first change). On "kept" a plain cut to the plumber alone, close, shrugging, the same plate.
A plain cut to the plumber, close, talking. The plate: HIS ACCOUNT:. On "held" a plain cut to the homeowner on the phone, cross, and a new plate lands: SHE PUT THE / JOB ON HOLD, the last row red.
A plain cut to the plumber, close, with the clipboard. The plate: HIS EXAMPLE: / 1-TRUCK SHOP. On "nine" it gives way to a stamp: OF EVERY $100 / $9 LEFT, the last row big and gold.

His example invoice on the left over the dimmed kitchen, the plumber close on the right holding the clipboard (she is not in it): a cream card headed EXAMPLE $100 in red, one row landing under it as each is said: TECH $41, then on "Sixteen" OFFICE PAY $16, on "eight" TRUCK $8, on "Twenty" OVERHEAD $20, on "Six" INS + HOME $6; then the plumber gestures at it and a gold band steps down the five rows, one at a time, until the cut.
A plain cut to the plumber in the kitchen, close, talking. The plate: NO RENT: / $9 LEFT, the last row big and gold.
A plain cut to the plumber, close. The plate: $9 LEFT, struck through in red as he says "shop"; on "two" he shrugs and it gives way to a stamp: WITH A SHOP: / UNDER $2, the last row big and red.

The frame splits, one person a side: the plumber on a slate left, the homeowner on wine right, arms folded. Left plate: PLUMBER, then FAIR? / UNDER $2 under it. Right plate: CLIENT, then on "too" TOO / MUCH? under it.
The plumber points down at the viewer; the homeowner keeps her arms folded. Both plates hold. Ends 1 s after the last word.
